title: Isometry Groups of Right Invariant Metrics in Geometric Quantum Complexity
abstract: In this paper, we give a complete description for the full isometry groups of a class of right invariant Riemannian metrics on the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2^N)$. These metrics have been used by physicists to study Nielsen's geometric approach for complexities in quantum computations.
summary: This paper provides a complete mathematical description of the isometry groups for specific right-invariant metrics on the special unitary group SU(2^N). By analyzing the symmetries of these metrics, the authors provide deep structural insights into the geometric framework used to define and study quantum computational complexity.
main_problem: The paper determines the full isometry groups of a specific class of right invariant Riemannian metrics defined on the special unitary group SU(2^N). This analysis is crucial for understanding the geometric structure used to define quantum complexity.
main_result: The full isometry group is found to be isomorphic to a semidirect product involving SU(2N) and components related to permutations and internal symmetries: Isom(G, g) is isomorphic to SU(2N) $times \{(	ext{SO}(3)^N times \mathbb{Z}_2) times 	ext{S}_N\}$.
method: The authors use techniques from differential geometry on Lie groups, analyzing the structure of the isometry group by examining how potential isometries must preserve the metric and the associated curvature tensor.
model_or_system: The physical system is quantum computation, modeled by unitary operators $U \in 	ext{SU}(2^N)$ acting on $N$ qubits. The complexity is quantified using a right-invariant Riemannian metric, specifically a 'penalty metric' $g_q$, on the group manifold.
key_observables: Geometric quantum complexity (distance between $U$ and identity), and the structure of the isometry group $	ext{Isom}(G, g)$.
important_parameters: The penalty factors $q_I$ defining the metric, and the number of qubits $N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to 'penalty metrics' $g$ on $	ext{SU}(2N)$ that satisfy specific conditions related to the preservation of weight-1 generators.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general results on isometry groups of right-invariant metrics on Lie groups, applies these tools to the specific case of $	ext{SU}(2N)$ with penalty metrics, and culminates in determining the explicit structure of the isometry group via analysis of the differential action on the Lie algebra.
why_interesting: The geometric approach to quantum complexity is a major theoretical tool. Understanding the symmetries (isometries) of the underlying metric space is fundamental, as these symmetries dictate which transformations preserve the notion of 'distance' or 'complexity' in the quantum computational model.
